scope: Jicamarca local child topology: Río Seco and Huaycoloro monitoring/convergence relation
purpose: Freeze bounded documentary topology that constrains the QUEBRADA→RÍO COLECTOR model without inventing a confluence coordinate, outlet, routing parameter, discharge, threshold or receiver overflow.

sources.title: Diseño e implementación de un sistema de alerta temprana para aluviones en el Radio Observatorio de Jicamarca
sources.bounded_section: 3.2 Determinación de puntos de monitoreo, PDF pages 57-58 as indexed by the public repository text layer
bounded_findings: The document explicitly treats Río Seco and Huaycoloro as two channels that converge.
The monitoring design places one measurement point after the channel union and another on the Río Seco channel to distinguish source contribution.
The document reports an approximate 100 m separation between monitoring points as instrumentation-design context.
The document reports an approximate 680 m field-to-ROJ communications distance as communications-design context.
forbidden_interpretations: The approximate 100 m monitoring-point separation is not an IRFEN travel time, attenuation, outlet distance or hydraulic parameter.
The approximate 680 m communications distance is not a channel length, routing distance, hydraulic parameter or receiver distance.
The monitoring design does not provide an exact confluence coordinate in the bounded text and cannot be converted into one by approximation.

bounded_findings: The official IGP page describes the Radio Observatorio de Jicamarca as located at the junction of the Río Seco and Huaycoloro quebradas in Lurigancho-Chosica.
forbidden_interpretations: The institutional location description is not an exact hydrologic confluence coordinate.
The observatory location is not itself an outlet, event footprint, hydraulic section or river-overflow observation.
